references.text: God explains why Phinehas's action was righteous and gives him a covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood as a reward for his zeal.
Eleazar, Phinehas's father, is mentioned here as the son of Aaron and ancestor of the priestly line.
The psalmist refers to Phinehas's action and how it stopped the plague and was credited to him as righteousness for all generations.
Phinehas later participates in the war against the Midianites as a priest, demonstrating his continued role as a leader in Israel.
Phinehas acts as the head of a delegation in a later conflict, showing his authority and position in Israel.
Phinehas's lineage is documented here as part of the Levitical priestly inheritance.
